title: Oncall Field Kit and Evidence Telemetry Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary:
This playbook defines the Oncall Field Kit: a compact, repeatable set of telemetry views, artifact-capture steps, and action templates that oncall engineers use to establish incident context and preserve evidence for post-incident review. It focuses on fast triage (first 15 minutes), controlled mitigation, and durable evidence collection to support RCA, SLO/error-budget accounting, and customer escalations.

Scope:
- Services: model-serving clusters, inference routing, cache layers (prefix/KV cache), autoscaling controller, and API gateway.
- Audiences: oncall engineers, incident commanders (ICs), SRE reviewers, and postmortem authors.
- Not included: detailed product bug triage and engineering design decisions outside immediate incident context.

Goals:
1) Reduce time-to-clear actionable context to 15 minutes for Tier 1 outages.
2) Ensure a minimum evidence artifact set is captured before mitigation actions that disrupt telemetry (e.g., node-fail reboots, rolling restarts).
3) Provide a lightweight checklist that integrates with our alerting, tracing, and logging stacks.

Definitions:
- Field Kit: the set of dashboards, queries, run commands, and one-line templates an oncall engineer uses when responding to alerts.
- Evidence Artifact: any saved dashboard snapshot, logs export, trace span set, config diff, or traffic capture used in the post-incident review.
- Action Template: a pre-approved mitigation or rollback step tied to specific SLO thresholds.

Oncall Field Kit Components (core):
- Telemetry dashboard links (pre-built):
  - API Gateway Overview (errors, 95/99 latency, request volume)
  - Inference Runtime Health (GPU queue depth, active sessions, KV cache hit rate)
  - Autoscaler & Pod Events (scale events, OOMs, image pull errors)
  - Latency Distribution (p50/p95/p99 by model-version and route)
  - Error Budget Burn Rate (per-tenant and global)
- Quick queries: Prometheus, Traces, and Logs (examples below)
- Evidence checklist (required artifacts)
- Action templates (tiered by error budget state)
- Preservation commands (how to capture artifacts reliably)

Required evidence checklist (capture these before disruptive mitigation whenever possible):
1) Dashboard snapshot (API Gateway Overview) — save as PNG and attach to incident ticket.
2) Prometheus alert window query: example below — copy results to ticket.
3) Representative logs export for 10 minutes before alert from API gateway and runtime nodes.
4) Trace snippet(s) for 5–20 slow requests (span IDs).
5) Recent deployment/config diffs (gitops commit IDs, manifests).
6) Autoscaler event log (scale-up/scale-down events, timestamps).
7) If applicable, tenant/route specific metrics (embedding vs. generation traffic).

Prometheus / Loki / Tracing example queries (copy-ready):
- Error rate: sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="api-gateway",status=~"5.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="api-gateway"}[5m]))
- p99 latency per model route: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="inference-runtime"}[5m])) by (le,route,model_version))
- KV cache hit rate: sum(rate(kv_cache_hits_total[5m])) / sum(rate(kv_cache_lookups_total[5m]))
- Logs (Loki): {app="inference-runtime"} | json | status=~"5.." | line_format "{pod} {status} {message}" | limit 500
- Trace sampler: service:inference-runtime and tag:route=<route> and duration>1000ms

Action templates (use only after evidence artifacts are captured):
- Tier 1 — Rapid mitigation (error budget burn > 20%/hour for a critical SLO OR global p99 spike > 3x baseline):
  1. Route traffic to degraded fallback model variant (router command): rrouter shift --from model-v2 --to model-v1 --pct 100 --reason "p99 spike"
  2. If fallback not available: enable ingress rate-limiter for non-critical tenants (see template 'ingress-throttle-noncritical')
  3. Scale inference-worker pool by +50% via autoscaler override: k8s patch deployment inference-worker -p '{"spec":{"replicas":<current*1.5>}}'
  4. Record actions and attach immediate evidence snapshots.
- Tier 2 — Controlled rollback (deploy/regression suspected):
  1. Validate deployment commit IDs and checksum.
  2. Roll back to previous stable revision: gitops rollback --service inference-runtime --to <stable-commit> --reason "observed regression"
  3. Monitor p95/p99 for 10 min; abort rollback if other systems degrade.

Error budget handling policy (quick reference):
- Green: burn rate < 5%/hour — standard incident process.
- Amber: burn rate between 5% and 20%/hour — oncall escalates to SRE lead; consider conservative mitigations (throttles, cache priming).
- Red: burn rate > 20%/hour — invoke Tier 1 rapid mitigation templates and notify Product and CS leads.

Preservation commands and locations:
- Dashboard snapshot: UI -> Share -> Export PNG. Save to incident ticket and to S3 prefix: s3://redwood-incident-artifacts/<incident-id>/dashboards/
- Prometheus data export: curl -g "https://prometheus.internal/api/v1/query_range?query=<expr>&start=<ts>&end=<ts>&step=15" > /tmp/prom_<incident-id>.json
- Logs bulk export (Loki): use loki query range CLI and save to s3. Example: loki query --query='{app="inference-runtime"}' --start=<start> --end=<end> --limit=10000 > /tmp/logs_<incident-id>.ndjson
- Traces: download spans from Jaeger/Tempo by trace IDs. Attach JSON to ticket.
- Config diff: git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD && git show <commit> > /tmp/commit_<id>.patch

Minimal incident timeline template (first 60 minutes):
1) 0-5m — Alert ack, populate incident ticket (title, service, initial symptoms), run Field Kit telemetry queries.
2) 5-15m — Attach evidence checklist items 1–3; determine if error budget condition is amber or red.
3) 15-30m — Apply action template (if required); note all commands and actor usernames.
4) 30-60m — Stabilize and hand off to investigator; ensure evidence artifacts are preserved.

Post-incident handoff and artifacts required for review:
- Incident ticket with timeline and attached artifacts (dashboards, logs, traces, git diffs).
- Root cause hypothesis and confidence level.
- SLO impact calc: show how much error budget was consumed (example below).
- Follow-up actions and owners (by-week deadlines).

SLO impact example (copy template):
- SLO: inference-api availability 99.9% monthly (target).
- Window: incident from 2026-01-10T14:07:00Z to 2026-01-10T14:42:00Z (35 minutes).
- Minutes in month: 44640. Downtime minutes: 35 -> availability impact = 35 / 44640 = 0.078% -> relative burn on monthly budget = 0.078 / 0.1 = 78% of monthly error budget.

Automation and tooling guidance:
- Integrate Field Kit into the oncall Slack channel: /oncall field-kit fetch <service> posts dashboard links and the common queries.
- Use incident CLI to bootstrap ticket and attach evidence: rw-incident create --service inference-runtime --attach-dashboards --preserve-logs 10m
- Where possible, use read-only snapshots to avoid changing live telemetry while collecting evidence.

Ownership and responsibilities:
- Initial oncall engineer: run Field Kit, collect artifacts, and apply Tiered action templates.
- IC during major incidents: coordinate mitigations and stakeholder comms.
- Postmortem owner: ensure evidence artifacts are complete and SLO impact calc included.
- SRE Tooling team: maintain dashboard templates, CLI integrations, and retention patterns.

Retention and compliance:
- Evidence artifacts are retained in s3://redwood-incident-artifacts for 180 days by default. If incident is security or customer-sensitive, set confidentiality = restricted and follow Security & Compliance escalation.

Appendix A — Quick reference table (links and thresholds):
| Item | Link / Command | Threshold / Note | Owner |
|---|---|---:|---|
| API Gateway dash | https://dashboards.internal/d/api-gateway | p99 > 3000ms | Platform Observability |
| Error budget query | PromQL (see body) | burn > 20%/hour = RED | SRE Lead |
| Snapshot location | s3://redwood-incident-artifacts/<id>/ | save PNG + JSON | Oncall |
| Rollback command | gitops rollback --service | use only with IC approval | Deploy Team |

Appendix B — Evidence capture troubleshooting:
- If Dashboard UI is unresponsive, use curl to export panel JSON and render with offline tooling.
- If Prometheus is rate-limited, use longer step sizes and narrow label selectors to reduce cardinality.
- If traces are sampled heavily, reduce sampler rate temporarily for affected routes (coord. with SRE Tooling).
